subject: Performance SLO qualification follow-up \u0014 latency/throughput targets & cost levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification follow-up  latency/throughput targets & cost levers

Thanks for the call today, Daniel  great to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements and what well validate in the spike.

Summary of requirements (from the call)  please confirm/correct:
- P95 end-to-end token latency target: <= 350ms for typical prompt sizes (~64 tokens) for our chat use-case.
- Throughput: baseline 500 requests/sec with steady-state bursts to 2,000 req/sec.
- Concurrent sessions: ~150 active concurrent websocket streams (many with streaming token-by-token).
- Streaming requirement: token-level streaming for UI (low tail latency is important).
- Payloads: average output length ~80 tokens, occasional long generations to 512 tokens.

Initial cost/performance levers we discussed to hit the SLO:
- Continuous batching windowing tuned for short (64128 token) responses to increase GPU utilization while preserving tail latency.
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated context to avoid re-encoding shared system prompts.
- Model variants: evaluate a smaller, quantized variant for high-volume routes (e.g., 70B q4_0) and fall back to full FP16 70B for heavy-context or quality-critical flows.
- Quantization profiles: test Q4 and Q5 profiles and measure quality delta on your eval set.
- Autoscaling + reserved capacity for steady baseline with burst capacity for peak traffic.

Requested deliverables from Redwood for the spike (we can run these in a 2-week technical POC):
1) Benchmark: P50/P95/P99 latency matrix across sequence lengths (64/128/512) for the two candidate model variants (quantized & FP16) under 1) single-req, 2) 50/150 concurrent streams, and 3) 500/2000 rps simulated load.
2) Cost estimate: token-level unit cost for both steady-state and burst traffic given suggested batching & caching profiles.
3) Implementation notes for streaming: recommended websocket concurrency settings, op-level batching window, and cache TTLs.

Attaching a proposed mutual action plan + a preliminary benchmark template to populate.

Next steps:
- You: confirm the targets above and whether we should include any stricter SLOs (e.g., P99 target).
- We: kick off benchmarking once you confirm, timeframe ~10 business days for the initial matrix.

Thanks  Ill loop in Rishi & Neha for technical coordination.

Marissa

From: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification follow-up  latency/throughput targets & cost levers

Thanks Marissa  this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- P95 350ms is our target for the interactive UI. Wed like P99 < 700ms if possible, but we understand thats aggressive for long generations.
- Throughput: 500 rps is our normal steady baseline; 2k rps is a hard peak (marketing campaigns). For capacity planning include a simulated spike of 5k rps for 10 minutes to see autoscaling behavior.
- Concurrency: 150 concurrent streaming sessions is the typical day peak; however, many sessions are short-lived.

Also: quality bar  we can tolerate a small degradation on QA metrics when moving to a quantized model for the high-volume route as long as we have a clear rollback path and automated A/B quality checks.

Well prioritize the P95/P99 numbers for UI flows. ProcureOps is looped for SLA/billing questions  Elena will own the procurement timeline.

Quick Q: for streaming, do you have guidance on recommended websocket idle timeouts (we currently set 60s)?

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification follow-up  latency/throughput targets & cost levers

Looping in a quick tech note for the POC plan:
1) Batching: we should tune continuous-batching with a small max window (1020ms) and an adaptive early-release for low-load tails to preserve interactive latency. That typically gives ~1.52.5x throughput improvement for 64128 token responses with minimal P95 impact.
2) Streaming: websocket idle timeout 60s is fine; recommend client heartbeats and server-side keepalive to release KV cache entries for truly idle sessions. For token-level streaming we keep a separate hot-path to avoid blocking batch assembly.
3) Caching: prefix/KV cache for system prompts and recent convo context  set TTL to 515 minutes depending on session churn. Cache hits can reduce compute by ~30% for chat scenarios with repeated instructions.
4) Quantization/model variants: plan tests for 1) FP16 70B, 2) q4_0 70B, 3) q5_1 70B-smaller. We’ll run both latency and eval-suite QA to measure tradeoffs.
5) Autoscaling: recommended baseline reserved capacity to cover 6070% of steady usage; burst via node autoscaling + ephemeral spot capacity attached to a burst pool. This keeps cost reasonable while preserving SLO.

Ill assemble the exact benchmark config (seed prompts, concurrency patterns, script) and drop it into the shared folder once Marissa confirms.

Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification follow-up  latency/throughput targets & cost levers

Thanks  all good. Confirming next steps and owners:
- Redwood (Rishi + Neha): populate and run the benchmark matrix (P50/P95/P99) across 64/128/512 token lengths for the three model profiles. Deliverable: CSV + short writeup with recommended production config and cost estimate. ETA: 10 business days from confirmation.
- Acme (Daniel + Elena): confirm whether P99 700ms should be a hard SLA for the initial rollout or an aspirational goal. Also confirm whether ProcureOps wants the cost estimate formatted for a procurement line item.
- Mutual: 1-hour readout session after the initial benchmark (will propose time once we have results).

Operational notes:
- For streaming we’ll default to 60s websocket idle, recommend client heartbeats every 20s.
- We’ll include an automated A/B quality check harness in the POC to detect regressions for quantized models; if QA drop >2% on your eval set we won’t recommend rolling to quantized for that route.

Please reply with any changes; otherwise we’ll kick off Friday morning.

Best 
Marissa
